description: Validity audit of the SDB Lite presenter_voice_control family (lite_presenter_a, lite_presenter_b), run 2026-09-29 in three rounds by LLM agents, following the protocol of audit_record.json. Rounds 1 and 2: per scenario a blind program re-derivation and a blind hand walk (public states only, compared with the stored references only after deriving), a code-versus-text audit and a partial/final review; findings grouped and each group judged by three lenses. Round 3: the four blind re-derivations on the final text, which is the text of data/lite/v1 (dataset hash fdfdd55d...). Fixes between rounds are listed; they changed reference answers only where listed. Long reasoning texts are omitted.

checks.agreement:
First-run agreement for lite_presenter_a is complete: consumed decisions 60/60 and all questions 360/360 (compare.py output: "consumed-decision agreement 60/60; all-question agreement 360/360"). I did not change the derivation after comparing, and nothing disagreed, so there was nothing to reconcile.

Method: I read only public/lite_presenter_a.json. prepared.rules, deck and session are identical in all 60 states. I wrote paper/notes/scratch-archive/presenter-audit/work/blind_lite_presenter_a/derive.py, which works each state out from that state alone, with no carry-over between ticks. It does five things:
- A general command parser. It splits sentences at . ? !, rejects a sentence ending in '?' or containing quotation marks, lower-cases it, deletes commas, apostrophes and a closing . or !, then allows one optional lead-in word, exactly one command phrase and an optional 'please'. It covers the slide phrases, go-to by number or by NAME with an optional trailing 'slide', and the play, pause, close and session phrases.
- A speaker-permission table (who may issue which command).
- A replay of final commands ordered by (final_at, at, sentence order).
- The early pause: in clip mode, a Presenter partial whose whole text is a pause command pauses the clip.
- ONSET captions, the question card counted over Audience utterances with at greater than the opening's at, and a host cue that matches 'back to you' as whole words after deleting apostrophes and dropping quoted text.
Output: work/blind_lite_presenter_a/derivation.json.

Derived timeline:
- Mode: talk at t0-16, clip at t17-32, talk at t33-45, questions at t46-57, closed at t58-59.
- Slide: s5 at t0-3, s6 at t4-9, s11 at t10-14, s7 at t15-39, s12 at t40-59.
- Clip state: play at t17-21, pause at t22-26 (the early pause 'hold it' at t22, then the final at t23; the partial 'sure play it' at t26 does not resume the clip), play at t27-28, pause at t29 (early pause 'pause the demo'), play at t30-32 (the early pause lapses; the partial 'back to the slides' at t32 changes nothing).
- Host cue: stand_by at t36 (the partial 'sends it back to you'), listen at t37-41, stand_by at t42-44, listen at t45 (the Host utterance h45 begins).
- Question card: waiting at t46-47, listening at t48-49, repeat at t50-52 (the partial 'the question is whether' at t52 does not count), answer at t53-57.
- Captions follow the newest at: clip at t19-21, audience at t24-25 and t48-51, host at t45-47 and t57-59.

The episode's traps are all resolved the same way by the rules and by the reference:
- partial commands at t3, t5, t8-9, t13-14, t16, t32, t39, t45 and t57;
- the non-command 'Next slide shows the demo, ...' at t7;
- the Clip soundtrack saying 'Next slide.' at t21, which carries no permission;
- the Audience request 'Can you play it again?' at t24-25;
- the quoted "next slide" at t35;
- the lexical 'back to you' at t36 that is then revised away;
- 'Thank you, Mira.', which is not the 'lets thank' command, at t46.

State consistency (checked with a script):
- Every snapshot's clock matches its index.
- at values are unique and in increasing order, and each utterance_id matches its at.
- final_at is never earlier than at and never later than the current tick, and it is set exactly when final is true.
- Finals never change afterwards.
- Partials use only lower-case letters and spaces ('thats', 'eleven').
- Each speaker has at most one partial, and it is that speaker's newest utterance.
- c21 appears already final, which the rules allow for short utterances.

The story holds together: she says 'first one more number', jumps to s11, then returns to the demo. No state inconsistencies were found.

checks.description: code-versus-text audit of the family's reference implementation
checks.agreement: No model run is part of this task, so the first-run agreement numbers don't apply and consumed_agreement is -1. What I checked: reference(state) reproduces all 120 stored golds (60 per scenario). tests/test_lite_presenter.py passes (20 tests). validate_episode gives 24 and 22 decision transitions, which match docs/lite/presenter.md. I read every rule sentence in RULES, all six question prompts and both deployment texts against _units, _command, FORMS, _replay, _words/_contains and reference(). I copied real states and ran each divergence through the reference with uv run python (scripts: scratchpad/cf_presenter.py and scratchpad/cf2.py). To test the stored answers, I wrote a second reference (scratchpad/alt_reading.py) that switches every divergence to its other reading. It splits a sentence at every terminator, treats a sentence that touches any single- or double-quoted span as quoted, allows a leading 'please', drops all punctuation except '?', and counts 'back to you' per sentence with single quotes ignored. It takes the opening at the Host final's final_at, lets a newer unrepeated Audience question count, and allows an open after closed, with and without resetting a second opening. It gives 0 differences on all 720 stored answers (2 scenarios x 60 ticks x 6 questions), so no divergence changes a stored answer in lite_presenter_a or lite_presenter_b. The data never uses single quotes as quotation marks, '!?', a leading 'please', a colon or dash in a command sentence, a second or post-closed opening, overlapping onsets, a trailing non-question Audience utterance, a Presenter-relayed request, or non-ASCII names. Some behaviours match the text but are easy to misread (not reported as issues): 'Go back to the slides.' is not a close (s7 clip keeps playing). 'Go to the next slide.' is not a command. 'OK,' is not a lead-in ('okay' is). 'Okay, so the question is ...' and 'Sorry, the question is ...' do not count as repetitions (two lead-ins, or a non-lead-in word). 'Go to slide 3.5.' goes to s3 because '.' ends a sentence. The Host's 'Thank you, Mira.' is not the closing thanks. A Presenter 'Play it.' on a clip slide during questions leaves questions for clip, and after 'Back to the slides.' it returns to talk, not questions. The rules say exactly this.

checks.description: partial/final review of the streaming-ASR conventions, revisions and evidence tiers
checks.agreement:
Not a blind first run, so consumed_agreement is -1. After the dump I worked out all 120 composed decisions (60 per scenario) again by hand from R1-R9 and agree with the stored gold at every tick. Every tick has one defensible answer under R2, R4, R7 and R9, so there are no reference_answer issues.

R1 compliance holds for every hypothesis (checked in Python):
- partials match [a-z ]+ with numbers spelled out
- at is unique
- each speaker has at most one partial, and it is that speaker's newest utterance
- replacement is in place under a fixed utterance_id and at
- finals never change, and at <= final_at <= now
- no utterance ever disappears

Revision inventory:
- Real word revisions: A p8 "go to slide one" -> "eleven"; A p29 "pause the demo" -> "because the demo runs on"; B h23, where the partial "sorry ines one question" drops "lets take" and the final restores it.
- A p36 ("back to you" -> "your") and B p38 ("you" -> "youlton") are word-extension growth.
- Everything else is prefix growth or final formatting (digits, punctuation, quotes).
- The only utterance that appears already final is A c21 (Clip "Next slide.").

Tier checks:
- Naive policies scored against the composed gold: ignoring partials gives 46/60 (A) and 48/60 (B); treating partials as finals gives 47/60 and 52/60. Both tiers are penalised in both scenarios.
- Partial words, as opposed to onset alone, change the gold at only 8 ticks: A 22, 29, 36, 42 and B 11, 15, 38, 52.

Counterfactual probes (scratchpad/pfreview/*.py and cf.py):
- overlapping Clip speech under the early pause
- a Host interruption while the Presenter's partial runs
- an abandoned (empty) Audience final
- an early pause that lapses at a final
- an already-final Presenter command
- a stand-by with a newer Audience utterance
- the phrase "get back to you" in a final
- finals arriving out of order

The proposed edits (issues 1, 3, 4 and 5) were rebuilt in scratch. They keep every R1 invariant, all 20 existing tests in tests/test_lite_presenter.py pass, and gold changes only where stated.

Files reviewed:
- src/streamdecisionbench/lite/tasks/presenter.py
- docs/lite/presenter.md
- tests/test_lite_presenter.py

grouped_findings.title: [blind:presenter_a, walk:presenter_b] host_cue question instruction leaves out the whole-word qualifier that the 'back to your' and 'back to Youlton' traps depend on

[blind:presenter_b, walk:presenter_b, blind:presenter_a] Rules never say what slide (and play) commands do in questions or closed mode, and the slide instructions' word 'questions' collides with the mode name
[blind:presenter_a, walk:presenter_a] 'closes the session by thanking the presenter' reads looser than the thanks command, and 'Thank you, Mira.' sits on that gap
[blind:presenter_b] The 'the question is' test depends on sentence splitting, but 'sentence' is defined only under Command form
[walk:presenter_a, walk:presenter_b, audit:presenter] question_card instruction is looser than rule 8 (newest Audience utterance, lead-in word, 'began after it')
[walk:presenter_a, walk:presenter_b] Host-cue whole-word match does not say how case and punctuation are handled
[blind:presenter_a, blind:presenter_b] clip_state 'latest final play or pause' is not tied to Presenter commands that took effect
[blind:presenter_a, asr:presenter] The lexical 'contains back to you' stand-by fires on phrases that are not handbacks, and the criteria gloss implies a real handoff
[blind:presenter_b, audit:presenter] 'Began after the opening' and 'began after it' do not say whether they compare onsets (at) or finals (final_at)
[audit:presenter] 'Open-questions gives questions from any mode' conflicts with 'after closed only slide commands apply'
[blind:presenter_a] 'demo' is both a slide NAME and a clip NOUN; the answers rely on reading 'Go back to the demo.' as a slide command
[blind:presenter_b] Other misreadings the rules rule out but a quick reader might take
[audit:presenter] Quoted text spanning several sentences still issues commands (rule 3 vs rule 4)
[audit:presenter] Only double quotes count as quotation marks, for both commands and the host cue
[audit:presenter] A second Host opening while already in questions mode resets the opening
[audit:presenter] A run of terminators forms one sentence ('Next slide!?')
[audit:presenter] 'please' is accepted only after the command phrase
[audit:presenter] The command parser keeps punctuation that the word matchers drop, so one transcript gets two normalisations
[audit:presenter] 'back to you' matches across sentence breaks and hyphens
[audit:presenter] The 'relayed words change nothing' clause has no code
[audit:presenter] Number parsing: spelled-out and odd digits are accepted, and a superscript digit crashes the reference
[audit:presenter] The thanks command accepts only [a-z] first names
[audit:presenter] Wording outside the rules: A's 'speakers ask for slides' and the docs' 'closing period'
[asr:presenter] Tier wording in R2 and in the question texts does not match R9 or the docs
[asr:presenter] R2's tier principle reads as a carve-out for the early pause, and it gives no reason why the repeat card waits for FINAL
[walk:presenter_b, asr:presenter] No overlapping speech, so the rule clauses for concurrent speakers and final_at ordering are never tested
[asr:presenter] Abandoned or retracted hypotheses are undefined
[asr:presenter] Tests do not check the transcript invariants that rule out abandoned partials, and do not cover overlap or an early-pause lapse at a final
[asr:presenter] The early pause only ever lapses at a revised partial, never at a final
[walk:presenter_a, blind:presenter_b] Coverage gaps: several rule paths are never exercised in either episode
[asr:presenter] The partial revision 'go to slide one' -> 'eleven' has no acoustic or biasing basis
[asr:presenter] 'back to youlton' relies on an out-of-vocabulary place name coined to contain 'you'
[walk:presenter_b, asr:presenter] Minor ASR and narrative realism oddities (h23 word deletion, uneven final growth, quotes, number format, story consistency)
[asr:presenter] presenter.md says Ines 'holds' the animation in scenario B, but she never does

rounds.changes_after: Rule and question texts aligned (host cue, question card, clip state, reopening, thanks, sentence and word normalisation); stand-by narrowed to a sentence ending in 'back to you' (optionally the Host's first name); quotation marks removed (finals carry none); utterances never dropped (declared); overlaps added at A t28-30 and B t22-24 (reference change: captions at A t28 and B t22); B early pause lapses at a final; 'go to slide one' -> 'seven'; 'youlton' -> 'union street'.

checks.description: blind re-derivation: independent reimplementation of the public rules as a program
checks.agreement:
First run, blind: consumed decisions 60/60, all questions 360/360. The derivation was written before compare.py was run and was not changed afterwards.

Method: I wrote paper/notes/scratch-archive/presenter-audit2/work/blind_lite_presenter_a/derive.py from the public prepared.rules and the question text only. It computes each tick from that state alone, with no memory carried between ticks. It rebuilds the mode, slide and clip history each time by replaying final commands in order of final_at, then at, then sentence order. The command parser splits finals into sentences, normalises them as the rules say (optional lead-in, one phrase, optional please) and enforces who is allowed to issue each command. On top of that it computes captions (by ONSET, largest at), the early pause (from the whole text of a Presenter partial, CURRENT TEXT), question_card (only Audience utterances with at greater than the opening's at, and 'the question is' only from a final Presenter utterance) and host_cue (CURRENT TEXT; stand-by ends at the ONSET of a Host utterance). The output is derivation.json in the same folder.

Replay the program found: next slide at t4 (s5 to s6); go to slide 11 at t10; go back to the demo at t15 (s7, still talk); play the video at t17 (clip, playing); hold it there at t23 (paused); sure, play it at t27 (playing); back to the slides at t33 (talk); go to the thank you slide at t40 (s12); the Host's let's take questions at t46 (questions, opening h45 at 45); the Host's let's thank Mira at t58 (closed).

Commands that correctly do nothing: the Clip's 'Next slide.' at t21 (Clip speech never commands); the Audience's 'Can you play it again?' at t25 (another speaker, and it ends in '?'); and every command-looking partial (t3, t5, t14, t16, t26, t32, t39, t57), since partials never move anything except the early pause.

Trap ticks, all matched: early pause at t22 and t29, and its lapse at t30; clip_state stays pause at t26 even though the partial says 'sure play it'; stand_by on a partial at t36, undone at t37; stand_by at t42–44, ended by the Host's onset at t45; waiting at t46–47, which ignores a24 because it began before the opening; listening at t48–49; repeat at t50–52, since the partial 'the question is whether' at t52 does not count; answer from t53; captions at t29–31 go to the Presenter because p29 has the larger at, although c28 is still updating.

I found no alternative reading a careful reader could defend that would change a consumed decision in this episode. The only readings that would change one contradict text the rules state outright; they are listed in the issues as non-defensible.

First-run agreement on lite_presenter_a: 60/60 consumed decisions and 360/360 across all questions. I wrote the derivation before running compare.py and did not change it afterwards. Derivation: paper/notes/scratch-archive/presenter-audit2/work/walk_lite_presenter_a.json. The hand-walk table it was built from is walk_lite_presenter_a.src.txt in the same folder.

Method: I printed only the utterances that were new or revised at each tick, then applied the public rules by hand, one release at a time. Starting state was talk mode on slide s5.

Boundary ticks I checked:
- 3-4: partial "next slide", then final "Next slide, please." moves to s6 at tick 4.
- 5-7: partial "next slide" turns into "Next slide shows the demo, but first...", which is talk, not a command. Slide stays s6.
- 8-10: partial seven, then eleven; the final "Go to slide 11." gives s11 at tick 10.
- 13-15: "go back to the" becomes "Go back to the demo." This matches the slide phrase 'go back to the NAME', giving s7. It does not match a NOUN command.
- 16-17: the play partial has no effect. The final "Play the video." on s7, which has a clip, gives clip mode with the clip playing.
- 19-21: captions switch to clip. The Clip channel's "Next slide." at tick 21 arrives already final and has no effect, because Clip speech never commands.
- 22-23: partial "hold it" is an early pause at tick 22. The final "Hold it there." keeps it paused.
- 24-25: the Audience's "Can you play it again?" has no effect; captions show audience.
- 26: partial "sure play it" does not unpause, so the clip stays paused. At 27 the final "Sure, play it." resumes play.
- 28-30: Clip c28 and Presenter p29 are partial at the same time. Captions follow the largest at, so presenter at 29-30. The early pause from "pause the demo" at 29 lapses at 30 when the partial is revised to "because the demo runs on", and the state falls back to the play from p26.
- 32-33: the partial close is ignored. The final "Back to the slides." gives talk at s7.
- 36-37: the partial "...sends it back to you" gives stand_by at 36. The revision to "back to your phone" gives listen at 37.
- 39-40: "Go to the thank you slide." gives s12.
- 42-44: stand_by, first from the partial and then from the final sentence "Back to you, Tomas."
- 45: the Host's partial ends stand-by by ONSET (listen). Mode stays talk because the command is still partial.
